verdict: P101-REAL-GATE-REFUSES-AS-EXPECTED: on 9 real multi-sector SPOC hosts, 4 had >=2 sectors INDEPENDENTLY detecting the recovered period above the frozen SNR floor (cross-sector corroboration MEASURED on real photometry, not modelled); but all 9 are confirmed-planet systems, so the protocol's requireNotAlreadyKnown correctly vetoes every one and the gate returns tier none. The stitched-BLS recovered period matched a catalog planet within 2% for only 6/9 -- the p29/p30 period-selection bottleneck (the strongest stitched peak is often a harmonic or a different planet), which is exactly why cross-sector detection and novelty must remain SEPARATE measured axes. No novel, corroborated real candidate was reached; no claim earned. The counterfactual (novelty granted, all else real) still lands at none, proving the gate needs blend/PSF/alias + a prospective precision run + human sign-off, not one flipped axis.
